title: Day, Night and Seasons
seo_title: Year 6 Science: Day, Night and Seasons Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe the movement of Earth and other planets relative to the Sun and model how Earth's tilt, rotation on its axis and revolution around the Sun cause cycles of day and night and seasons (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 6 science worksheets on day, night and seasons: Earth's rotation, revolution and tilt, Australian seasons, day length in Hobart, Sydney and Darwin, and the Sun's height. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Spin gives day and night; tilt gives seasons.
key_sub: Earth spins once a day and orbits the Sun once a year with a tilted axis.
body_html:
How to think about it

Earth's rotation causes day and night. Its tilt, as it orbits the Sun, causes the seasons.

  • Earth spins on its axis once every 24 hours. The half facing the Sun has day.
  • Earth's axis is tilted. From December to February the southern hemisphere leans towards the Sun: Australian summer, longer days and a higher Sun.
  • From June to August it leans away: winter, shorter days and longer midday shadows. Seasons are not caused by distance from the Sun.
Example

Which season is July in Australia?

June to August is winter in the southern hemisphere

Answer: winter

Example

Why is a midday shadow shorter in December?

the Sun is higher in summer

Answer: the Sun is higher

Common mistakes

  • Thinking summer happens because Earth is closer to the Sun.
  • Using northern-hemisphere months (Australian summer is December to February).
  • Mixing up rotation (spin, one day) and revolution (orbit, one year).

faq.q: Why does Australia have summer in December?
faq.a: Earth's axis is tilted. In December the southern hemisphere leans towards the Sun, so sunlight is more direct and days are longer.

faq.q: What is the difference between rotation and revolution?
faq.a: Rotation is Earth spinning on its axis, which takes about 24 hours. Revolution is Earth travelling around the Sun, which takes about 365 days.

faq.q: Why does day length change more in Hobart than in Darwin?
faq.a: Hobart is much further from the equator. The further a place is from the equator, the bigger the change in day length between summer and winter.

items.q: Why is it colder in winter even though the Sun shines?
c: The Sun is further away in winter.
Sunlight hits the ground at a low angle and days are shorter.
The Sun gives off less light in winter.
Clouds always block the Sun in winter.
items.e: Low-angle sunlight spreads over a bigger area.

Why is it hot all year in Darwin?
c: It is close to the equator, so the Sun is high in the sky all year.
It is closest to the Sun.
It has the longest days in December.
items.e: Near the equator, sunlight is direct all year.

items.q: Which way does the Earth spin?
items.e: Day and night happen because the Earth spins; the Sun only seems to move.

items.q: How long does Earth take to travel once around the Sun?

items.q: First Nations peoples have many seasons in their calendars, such as six in parts of the Top End. What are these seasons based on?

items.q: Why do solar panels in Australia usually face north?

The midday Sun is in the northern part of the sky.

items.e: Facing the Sun collects the most light.

items.q: Mia's class measures the length of a stick's shadow every hour from 9 am to 3 pm. What should they keep the same?
